root_cause.text: In `drivers/crypto/ccp/ccp-ops.c`, `ccp_run_aes_gcm_cmd()` used the wrong cleanup annotation on a heap-allocated local pointer (`__cleanup(kfree)` instead of `__free(kfree)`), causing the stack address of the pointer variable to be passed to `kfree()` on scope exit.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `} *wa __cleanup(kfree) = kzalloc(sizeof *wa, GFP_KERNEL);` to `} *wa __free(kfree) = kzalloc(sizeof(*wa), GFP_KERNEL);`, and the CVE description states that `__cleanup(kfree)` “will make the address of the local variable, rather than the address returned by kmalloc, passed to kfree directly and lead to a crash due to invalid deallocation of stack address.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Switch the AES-GCM work area pointer to the newer automatic-free annotation while preserving the same allocation and cleanup behavior.
intent_record.what: The declaration of the local pointer `wa` in `ccp_run_aes_gcm_cmd()` was changed from using `__cleanup(kfree)` to `__free(kfree)`, and the `kzalloc` size expression was rewritten from `sizeof *wa` to `sizeof(*wa)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the allocated `wa` object is still automatically freed with `kfree` when it goes out of scope; the change switches to a different kernel-managed cleanup annotation without altering the allocation or deallocation behavior.

grouping_result.intent: Switch the AES-GCM work area pointer to the newer automatic-free annotation while preserving the same allocation and cleanup behavior.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes the AES-GCM work area pointer cleanup annotation from the wrong form to the newer automatic-free annotation, addressing the incorrect kfree-on-scope-exit issue.

candidates.rationale: This line uses the wrong cleanup annotation on a heap-allocated pointer variable. On scope exit it triggers kfree() on the address of the local pointer variable rather than the allocated heap object, causing invalid free and potential memory corruption.

vuln_statements.explanation: This declaration uses `__cleanup(kfree)` on a heap-allocated local pointer, which causes `kfree()` to be invoked on the stack address of the pointer variable when the scope exits instead of using the allocated object cleanup mechanism.
